prompt: I'm building a Flutter wardrobe app on fmodel-dart. My domain layer already exists. In lib/state_change/add_item/api.dart I have `final class AddItemCommand { const AddItemCommand({required this.name, required this.category}); final String name; final String category; }` and a `Decider<AddItemCommand, AddItemState, WardrobeEvent>` called `addItemDecider` that emits `ItemAddedEvent`. On the read side, lib/state_view/wardrobe_view/api.dart has a `View<WardrobeViewState, WardrobeEvent>` called `wardrobeView`, where `WardrobeViewState` holds `List<WardrobeItem> items`. There's an `EventSourcingAggregate` and a `MaterializedView` already created via the fmodel `create...` factories. Please wire an add-item screen's state management as a Cubit: the screen lets the user type a name + category and tap Add, then shows the updated list of items, a loading spinner while adding, and an error message if the domain rejects it. Give me the Cubit, its state class, and how to inject the fmodel service. Keep the naming clean — I don't want to confuse my domain events with anything on the UI side.
assertions: Presentation state class carries a Ui marker (e.g. AddItemUiState), never a bare AddItemState that collides with the domain write-model type name.
UiState render data is built from the read-model projection (WardrobeViewState), not from the Decider/aggregate write-model state.
Domain types (AddItemCommand, WardrobeViewState, ItemAddedEvent) are imported/referenced, not redefined in the presentation code.
Uses a Cubit (method-driven) rather than an event-driven Bloc for this 1:1 command screen.
UiState models status with an initial/loading/success/failure notion (enum or sealed states) and uses value equality (Equatable).
The application service or aggregate is injected via the constructor, not constructed inside the Cubit.
A domain rejection is surfaced by mapping DomainError to a failure UI state, not by letting it propagate to the widget.
